details: U.S. President Donald Trump reportedly earned more than $1.4 billion from his family's cryptocurrency ventures in 2025, according to his latest financial disclosures released around July 1, 2026. Much of this income stemmed from the sale of crypto tokens through World Liberty Financial, a firm co-founded by his sons, and royalties from a Trump meme coin. The news highlights how crypto has significantly boosted the president's wealth and underscores his administration's pro-crypto policies aimed at making the U.S. a leading crypto hub. Critics, however, have raised questions about potential conflicts of interest given his dual role as a beneficiary and a policymaker in the crypto space.
title: Trump's Crypto Ventures Generate Over $1.4 Billion in Income

details: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage is under investigation by a standards watchdog following allegations that he lobbied the Bank of England to abandon plans for a central bank digital currency (CBDC) that could negatively impact his party's billionaire crypto donor. Farage reportedly used a private meeting with Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey to advocate against a state-run digital pound, despite having received a substantial personal "gift" and party donations from a major shareholder in Tether, a prominent stablecoin company.
title: Nigel Farage Faces Scrutiny for Crypto Lobbying Efforts

details: A leading association of German banks has voiced strong opposition to a potential plan by the European Central Bank (ECB) to double the minimum reserve requirements for lenders from 1% to 2%. Reported on July 1, 2026, the ECB's consideration aims to reduce its interest expenses and mitigate inflation. However, German banks argue that such a move would act as a de facto tax, tying up liquidity, hurting profitability, and placing European banks at a competitive disadvantage globally, especially amidst growing geopolitical uncertainties.
title: German Banks Oppose ECB's Potential Reserve Requirement Hike
